items.summary: A couple of Walmart's budget-friendly smart home cameras will be able to recognize people around your house now using Google's familiar face detection feature. A new Google Home update brings Familiar Faces support to the $35 Onn Outdoor Camera Plug-In and $77 Onn Floodlight Came
items.content:
You can get Familiar Faces alerts from Walmart’s budget smart home cameras.﻿

A couple of Walmart’s budget-friendly smart home cameras will be able to recognize people around your house now using Google’s familiar face detection feature. A new Google Home update brings Familiar Faces support to the $35 Onn Outdoor Camera Plug-In and $77 Onn Floodlight Camera Hardwired. However, a Google Home Premium subscription is still required to access the feature.

Both cameras and Google’s Nest Cam Outdoor (wired, 2nd gen) also have a new remote control in the Google Home app you can use to start or stop a 30-second security siren while watching the camera’s live video feed.

Earlier this month, Google announced that Gemini Live would get an upgrade “to our latest speech-to-speech architecture for significantly faster response times and a smoother experience.” Now it says those improvements are rolling out over the coming weeks, along with new smart home control, as “Gemini Live now supports all your daily actions, from setting timers to turning off the lights.”

items.content:
핵심 아키텍처에서 모델 파생…"내년 세자릿수 톱스 공개"

반도체ㆍ디스플레이 입력 :2026/11/26 09:00

글로벌 피지컬 인공지능(AI) 시장의 실질적인 주류 연산 성능이 약 50톱스(TOPS·초당 1조회 연산)라는 목소리가 나왔다. 연산량을 무작정 키우기보다 배터리와 발열 제약 속에서 전력 대비 성능을 극대화해야 한다는 진단이다.

이광재 텔레칩스 전무는 최근 지디넷코리아 인터뷰에서 "휴머노이드 이전 단계로 현재 시장을 주도하는 자율이동로봇(AMR)과 상업용 서비스 로봇은 주변환경의 실시간 지도 작성(맵핑)과 장애물 회피 기능이 필수"라며 "이들 기기는 배터리로 구동해 발열과 전력 소모에 민감하다"고 말했다. 그러면서 "연산량을 높이는 대신 50톱스 미만에서 AI 모델을 소형화하고 전력 대비 성능을 높이는 흐름이 확산하고 있다"고 덧붙였다.

로봇과 에 지 기기가 수행하는 임무 난도에 따라 AI 칩 요구 성능은 세분화된다. 복합 임무를 처리하는 로봇에는 50톱스, 제한된 영역에서 단순 작업을 수행하는 로봇은 25톱스 수준이 적합하다. 드론은 20톱스 미만, 보안 CCTV는 그보다 낮은 성능으로도 단위 임무를 소화한다. 경찰 오토바이용 스마트 헬멧처럼 빠르게 이동하는 환경에서는 단순 연산량보다 실시간 응답성이 핵심이다.

글로벌 반도체 기업은 기존 주력 칩에서 피지컬 AI용 파생 모델을 만드는 전략을 택했다. 로봇 전용 칩을 백지 상태에서 새로 설계하는 것보다 이미 검증된 핵심 아키텍처를 유지한 채 열설계전력(TDP), 폼팩터, 내열성 등을 조정해 제품군을 다변화하고 소프트웨어를 최적화하는 방향이다. 엔비디아 젯슨 시리즈가 대표적이다. 퀄컴도 스마트폰용 반도체 기술을 바탕으로 차량·로봇·산업용 제품을 개발한다.

검증된 차량용 칩 아키텍처로 피지컬 AI 확장

텔레칩스도 전략이 같다. 자동차 시장에서 검증한 차량용 시스템반도체(SoC) 구조를 피지컬 AI와 로봇용으로 발전시켰다.

텔레칩스의 AI 칩 라인업은 통합 칩 돌핀과 파생 칩 엔돌핀 두 축이다. 돌핀은 그래픽처리장치(GPU)·중앙처리장치(CPU)·신경망처리장치(NPU)를 모두 담아 차량 콕핏의 중앙 관제 역할을 하며 안전과 편의 기능을 함께 처리한다. 엔돌핀은 NPU에 특화해 안전 기능에 집중한다.

자동차가 제한된 도로 환경 인식에 초점을 맞춘다면 로봇은 3차원 공간에서 다수 관절을 동시 제어해야 한다. 텔레칩스는 기존 차량용 칩 구조에 다중 센서와 모터 제어기 인터페이스를 강화했다. 또한 로봇 크기와 배터리 제약에 맞춰 소비전력과 발열을 제어하도록 제품군을 다각화했다.

이 전무는 "피지컬 AI는 AI 판단이 실제 기기 물리적 움직임으로 직결되는 기술"이라며 "실시간 환경 인식·판단을 위한 빠른 응답속도와 어떠한 환경에서도 오작동 없는 높은 신뢰·안전성이 필수"라고 강조했다. 이어 "이는 텔레칩스가 차량용 시스템반도체를 개발하며 최우선시한 칩 설계, 성능 기준과 일치한다"고 덧붙였 다.

전기차 시대에 축적한 전력 최적화 노하우도 텔레칩스 강점이다. 배터리 소모로 차량이 멈추는 응급 상황을 막기 위해 칩 자체는 물론 전체 시스템의 불필요한 전원을 차단하는 제어 메커니즘을 갖췄다. 상황에 따라 GPU나 NPU 가동을 줄여 전력 예산을 낮추는 기술은 배터리 기반 로봇에 그대로 적용한다.

내년 세 자릿수 톱스 생성형 AI 칩 출격

텔레칩스는 현재 8톱스급 AI 모듈로 무게와 배터리 제약이 큰 경량형 에지 기기 실증(PoC)을 수행하고 있다. 돌핀과 엔돌핀 칩 자체는 양산 단계지만 산업용 모듈은 실증 파트너사에 샘플을 제공했다.

이 전무는 "대구시 지자체 실증사업으로 스마트 시티용 드론에 8톱스 모듈을 테스트하고 있다"며 "드론 카메라로 교통정체, 교차로 사고, 지상 사각지대를 상공에서 포착한 뒤 에지 단에서 상황을 판단해 인프라와 관제센터로 전송한다"고 말했다.

경찰용 스마트 헬멧에는 엔돌핀 칩을 탑재해 테스트 중이다. 전방 카메라 인식은 물론 사용자 음성명령을 이해하고 네트워킹까지 처리한다.

내년에는 물류, 서비스, 공장 자동화 등 로봇 분야로 실증을 확대한다. 공장 현장에서는 2개 이상의 매니퓰레이터와 바퀴 달린 물류 로봇에 적용하는 방안을 파트너사와 논의할 예정이다.

차세대 반도체 로드맵 윤곽도 밝혔다. 이 전무는 "돌핀과 엔돌핀은 영상(비전) 인식에 특화했지만, 내년에 공개할 칩과 모듈은 생성형 AI까지 구동 가능할 것"이라며 "연산 성능은 기존 8톱스의 10배인 세 자릿수에 가까울 것"이라고 말했다. 생성형 AI를 지원해 로봇이 인간과 함께 작업하면서 자연어 명령을 수행하도록 만든다는 구상이다.

차세대 칩은 고객 맞춤형 사양으로 공급한다. 최상위 칩을 먼저 설계한 뒤 고객사 요구에 맞춰 성능과 전력 소모를 조정해 공급할 계획이다.

items.content:
저자는 미래의 불확실성을 예측 AI 시스템으로 분석하여 기업의 경쟁력을 강화하는 방법을 제시합니다. 데이터 기반의 정량적 분석으로 의사결정 속도를 높이고 시장 변화에 선제적으로 대응할 수 있는 실무 전략을 제공합니다.

올해는 생성 AI 활용서와 함께 수요와 재고, 원자재 가격을 어떻게 읽을지 다룬 책을 찾는 문의가 눈에 띈다. 내년 생산량과 발주 규모를 정하는 S&OP 회의가 몰리는 때다. 영풍문고 북마스터는 청림 출판이 지난 9월 펴낸 『불가능을 예측하라』를 골랐다.

책은 생성 AI가 답하지 못하는 질문에서 출발한다. 다음 달 수요가 늘어날지, 이 재고를 지금 발주해야 할지처럼 아직 일어나지 않은 결과를 숫자로 읽는 일이다. 책이 인용한 맥킨지 2025년 조사에서 AI를 정기적으로 쓰는 기업은 88%였지만, AI가 영업이익에 유의미한 영향을 줬다는 응답은 39% 였다.

저자는 이 틈을 '예측 AI'로 메우자고 말한다. 2부는 신제품 수요예측과 프로모션, 카니발라이제 이션 등 일곱 현장을, 3부는 모델·데이터·설명·시뮬레이션·에이전트의 다섯 엔진을, 4부는 조직 안의 저항과 회의 방식을 다룬다. 캐나다 스타트업 블루닷이 항공편 예약과 현지 기사 같은 비정형 데이터로 세계보건기구보다 먼저 코로나19의 전조를 짚은 사례처럼, 데이터에 없던 사건을 읽는 방법도 함께 다룬다.

저자 정두희는 한동대 AI융합학부 부교수이자 예측 AI 기업 임팩티브AI 대표다. 삼성경제연구소 SERI CEO 수석과 MIT 테크놀로지 리뷰 한국판 편집장을 지낸 뒤 2021년 창업했고, 제조·유통·식음료·반도체 등 85개 기업과 일했다고 밝힌다. 『3년 후 AI 초격차 시대가 온다』 같은 해설서를 써 온 저자가 이번에는 직접 시스템을 만들며 겪은 현장을 중심에 놓았다. 러시아-우크라이나 전쟁 뒤 급등한 니켈 가격을 LLM으로 비정형 데이터를 분석해 예측하려 한 사례가 대표적이다.

4부의 제안은 기술보다 조직에 가깝다. 예측 AI를 '도입'하지 말고 업무 흐름에 스며들게 하라는 것, 정확한 예측이 오히려 거부당하는 저항의 구조부터 이해하라는 것이다.

권기원 영풍문고 서적팀 팀장은 "숫자를 다루는 책이지만 4부의 회의 이야기가 오래 남는다. '누가 맞는가'에서 '무엇을 할 것인가'로 질문을 바꾸자는 대목은 경영진 독자에게 바로 통한다"고 말했다. 이원준 영풍문고 기술부문 MD는 "3부가 모델의 원리를 수식 없이 풀어 줘서, 데이터 조직과 현업이 같은 말로 이야기를 시작할 수 있다"고 평가했다.

내년 수요 계획을 놓고 영업·생산·재무가 각자의 숫자를 들고 마주 앉을 예정이라면, 의사결정 회의 를 다룬 4부 4장부터 함께 읽고 회의에 들어갈 만하다. 에필로그의 '엔진이 아니라 나침반이 되라'는 당부는 그 회의를 이끄는 리더에게 남기는 말이다.

- 청림출판 | 2026년 9월 9일 출간 | 316쪽 | 정가 20,000원

- ISBN 9788935215195

영풍문고는 1992년 종로에서 문을 연 이래 34년간 책과 독자를 이어온 서점입니다. 현재 전국 46개 지점과 온라인몰 을 운영하며, 100만명의 회원에게 도서와 문화 콘텐츠를 제공하고 있습니다.

미국 패스트푸드 체인 웬디스가 가맹점의 판매 데이터를 활용해 메뉴 가격을 인위적으로 높였다는 의혹으로 집단소송에 휘말렸다. 앞서 맥도날드도 비슷한 의혹으로 제소되는 등 외식 프랜차이즈의 가격 결정 방식을 둘러싼 논란이 커지고 있다.

24일(현지시간) 로이터에 따르면 미국 캘리포니아주에 거주하는 소비자 앤디 가르시아는 웬디스와 외식업 소프트웨어 업체 NCR 보익스를 상대로 메릴랜드주 연방법원에 집단소송을 제기했다.

원고 측은 웬디스가 NCR 보익스의 판매시점관리(POS) 시스템인 ‘알로하’를 통해 가맹점별 판매 및 가격 정보를 수집하고 공유했다고 주장했다. 서로 가격 경쟁을 해야 할 가맹점들이 본사의 통제 아래 메뉴 가격을 결정하면서 소비자들이 더 높은 가격을 지불하게 됐다는 설명이다.

원고 측은 웬디스가 수천개 가맹점과 직영점의 가격 결정에 관여했으며 이 같은 행위가 이르면 지난 2016년부터 이어졌다고 강조했다.

원고 측 변호인 앨런 뉴마크는 “웬디스는 투자자들에게 가맹점주가 자체적으로 가격을 결정한다고 설명해왔다”며 “서로 경쟁해야 할 사업자들이 가격 경쟁을 멈추면 소비자는 더 많은 돈을 지불하게 된다”고 말했다.

이번 소송은 최소 수만명의 웬디스 이용자를 대표해 제기됐다. 원고 측은 손해배상과 함께 웬디스의 가격 조정 행위를 중단하도록 법원에 명령을 내려달라고 요구했다.

웬디스와 NCR 보익스는 외신에 즉각 답변하지 않았다.

최근 미국에서는 외식 프랜차이즈가 데이터를 수집하고 소프트웨어를 활용해 메뉴 가격을 결정하는 방식이 법적 쟁점으로 떠오르고 있다고 외신은 소개했다.

앞서 맥도날드도 인공지능(AI)을 활용해 가맹점의 메뉴 가격 결정을 지원한다는 사실이 알려진 뒤 지난달 가격 담합 의혹으로 소송을 당했다. 맥도날드는 위법 행위 의혹을 부인했다.

26일 회사에 따르면, 에이뎁트는 개인의 AI 활용 역량을 평가하는 자격시험이다. 기업들이 채용과 임직원 역량 진단에 활용하는 프로그래머스 'AI 역량평가'와 동일한 평가 체계·기준을 적용했으며, 합격자에게 디지털 인증서와 링크드인 배지를 발급한다. 자격은 수준에 따라 ▲'AI 필수역량인증' 에이뎁트 에센셜 ▲'AI 전문역량인증' 에이뎁트 프로페셔널 2종으로 나뉜다.

에센셜은 실무에 필요한 기본 AI 활용 능력을 살피는 시험으로 50분간 객관식·단답형 문항을 치른다. AI로 업무 과제를 수행해 조건에 부합하는 결과물을 도출하고 AI 답변에서 사실과 다른 내용을 가려내는 능력을 평가하며, 합격 기준은 1000점 만점 기준 600점 이상이다.

프로페셔널은 복합 비즈니스 과제를 해결하는 심화 역량을 검증하는 시험으로 90분간 객관식·단답형·서술형 문항 및 작업형 실기 과제를 실시한다. 여러 자료 비교·분석과 AI 결과 오류 검증, 보안·윤리 기준 기반의 AI 업무 해결 방안 기획 역량을 평가하며 등급은 점수에 따라 1~4레벨로 산정된다.

1기 응시 접수는 내년 1월 13일까지 프로그래머스 에이뎁트 페이지에서 진행되며 첫 시험은 1월 17일 치러진다. 응시료는 에센셜 7만원·프로페셔널 9만원이며 1기 응시자 전원에게 50% 할인 혜택을 제공하고, 12월 16일까지 접수한 선착순 100명에게는 2기 시험 무료 재응시 기회를 준다.

임성수 그렙 대표는 "지난 3월 출시한 AI 역량평가를 6개월 만에 50여 개 기업·기관이 도입하거나 검토할 만큼 기업 채용 현장에서는 AI를 활용하는 능력과 함께 산출물의 정확성을 검증하고 책임질 수 있는 역량을 요구하고 있다"며 "에이뎁트는 기업 현장의 검증 기준을 개인에게도 적용한 자격시험인 만큼 구직자와 재직자가 AI 실무 역량을 객관적으로 입증하는 수단으로 자리 잡도록 운영하겠다"고 말했다.

items.content:
제네시스 첫 수상…아이오닉 3는 '올해의 소형차'

카테크 입력 :2026/11/26 08:44

제네시스가 영국 자동차 전문 매체 탑기어가 뽑은 '올해의 제조사'에 처음으로 이름을 올렸다. 현대자동차의 유럽 전용 전기차 아이오닉 3도 '올해의 소형차'에 선정되면서 현대자동차그룹은 6년 연속 수상 기록을 이어갔다.

현대차그룹은 지난 24일(현지시간) 발표된 '2027 탑기어 어워즈'에서 제네시스와 현대차 아이오닉 3가 각각 올해의 제조사와 올해의 소형차로 선정됐다고 26일 밝혔다.

탑기어는 해마다 주요 신차와 자동차 제조사를 대상으로 부문별 수상작을 선정한다. 올해의 제조사 부문은 탑기어 편집진이 브랜드 전반을 종합 심사해 수상자를 결정한다. 제네시스는 개별 차종의 상품성과 브랜드 전반의 완성도, 경쟁력에서 높은 평가를 받았다.

톰 포드 탑기어 부편집장은 제네시스의 미래지향적인 사고와 도전 정신을 높이 평가했다. 특정 모델의 성과보다 브랜드가 앞으로 나아갈 방향을 명확히 인식하고 있다는 점을 수상 배경으로 꼽았다.

제네시스가 탑기어 어워즈에서 상을 받은 것은 이번이 처음이다. 앞서 현대차는 2018년과 2021년, 기아는 2022년 올해의 제조사로 선정됐다. 이번 수상으로 현대차그룹의 세 브랜드가 모두 같은 부문에서 수상 기록을 갖게 됐다.

올해의 소형차에 뽑힌 아이오닉 3는 유럽 시장을 겨냥해 개발한 소형 전기 해치백이다. 탑기어는 가격과 공간 설계, 적재 공간, 주행 성능 등을 평가했다. 올리 큐 탑기어 부편집장은 한 대로도 일상에서 충분히 활용할 수 있다며 가격 대비 주행거리와 공간 활용성, 효율성을 강점으로 꼽았다.

아이오닉 3에는 공기역학적 효율과 실내 공간을 함께 확보하기 위한 '에어로 해치' 디자인이 적용됐다. 현대차는 전기차 전용 플랫폼 E-GMP를 기반으로 유럽 주행 환경에 맞춰 성능을 조율했다. 차세대 인포테인먼트 시스템 '플레오스 커넥트'도 탑재했다.

현대차그룹의 연속 수상은 2021년 시작됐다. 당시 현대차는 올해의 제조사와 i20 N의 올해의 차 수상으로 2관왕에 올랐고, 기아 EV6는 올해의 크로스오버에 선정됐다. 2022년에는 현대차 N 비전 74가 올해의 인기 차량에 올랐고 기아가 올해의 제조사로 뽑혔다.

2023년에는 현대차 아이오닉 5 N이 올해의 차, 기아 EV9이 올해의 패밀리카로 선정됐다. 2024년에는 현대차 싼타페가 올해의 스포츠유틸리티차(SUV), 기아 EV3가 올해의 크로스오버에 올랐다. 지난해에는 현대차 캐스퍼 일렉트릭이 올해의 경차, 기아 PV5 패신저가 올해의 패밀리카에 각각 이름을 올렸다.

현대차그룹 관계자는 "이번 수상은 세계적으로 권위 있는 자동차 전문 매체로부터 우수한 브랜드 경쟁력과 상품성을 인정받은 결과"라며 "앞으로도 혁신적인 기술과 차별화된 디자인을 바탕으로 고객에게 새로운 가치를 제공하기 위해 노력할 것"이라고 말했다.

운영팀은 지난 24일(현지시간) 공식 X를 통해 실물 무장 카드로 부대를 움직이는 게임 ‘영걸대전’의 대인전 등 점검 중인 서비스의 시험 가동 재개를 준비하고 있다고 밝혔다. 세가 페이브는 아케이드 게임과 완구를 개발·판매하는 세가그룹 계열사다.

일본판 리듬 게임 ‘츄니즘’과 ‘마이마이 디럭스’는 지난 21일부터 아이메를 이용한 플레이와 게임별 웹 서비스를 시험 재개했다. 츄니즘은 터치 슬라이더와 손을 들어 올리는 동작으로, 마이마이 디럭스는 원형 터치 화면과 주변 버튼으로 곡을 연주하는 게임이다.

두 게임의 일본판 운영팀은 25일 오전 7시부터 대상 이용자가 로그인하면 점검 보상을 받을 수 있다고 안내했다. 츄니즘은 맵 진행 3배 티켓과 캐릭터 경험치 9배 아이템을, 마이마이 디럭스는 지역 진행 5배 티켓과 1만 마일을 지급한다.

영걸대전 대인전과 한 기기에서 여러 게임을 제공하는 ‘ALL.Net P-ras MULTI’ 버전 2·3, 건슈팅 게임 ‘하우스 오브 더 데드 스칼렛 던’, 메달 게임 ‘빙고 시어터’는 우선 복구 대상이다. 운영팀은 27일 오전 9시께 다음 복구 상황을 안내할 예정이다.

items.title: S&P considers Nvidia credit downgrade over governance and ‘key man’ risks
items.summary: The credit rating agency may lower Nvidia's credit rating to AA-, the fourth-highest rating.
items.content:
S&P Global Ratings, one of the three major credit rating agencies, is considering downgrading Nvidia’s rating, citing concerns about the company’s management and governance practices.

Despite Nvidia’s strong financial performance, the ouster and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang has raised concerns about “weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning” and “key man risk,” meaning heavy reliance on Huang for its future success, S&P said in a statement .

The agency expects to finish its review within 90 days and could cut Nvidia’s rating from AA to AA-, the fourth-highest on its scale.

Although Nvidia is certain to keep its investment-grade rating, a downgrade could raise its borrowing costs. Because Nvidia backstops neoclouds and other infrastructure companies that lack strong credit on their own, a lower rating could make their debt costlier or force them to post more collateral.

In August, Nvidia announced plans to arrange $500 billion in financing for AI infrastructure with six financial institutions, including Goldman Sachs, Apollo, and Blackstone. Under the original terms, Nvidia would guarantee 25% of the loans. But even before Huang’s ouster and return, lenders had been demanding that Nvidia guarantee more, Bloomberg reported .

A downgrade would likely prompt lenders to demand even larger guarantees.

한국생산기술연구원(원장 손웅희)은 국립농업과학원(원장 성제훈)과 인공지능(AI)·로봇기술을 농업에 접목한 농업·산업기술 융합 연구를 위한 업무협약을 체결했다고 밝혔다.

생기원이 보유한 AI·로봇·자동화 등 첨단 산업기술에 농과원의 농업기술과 현장실증 역량을 결합해 실용적 융합기술을 개발한다는 구상이다.

두 기관의 협력은 지난해 9월 농과원 연구진이 생기원을 방문해 AI 제어와 에너지 관리 기술의 농업 활용 가능성을 논의하면서 물꼬를 텄다.

지난 1월부터 양파를 저장하기 전 건조 단계인 ‘예건’과 ‘저장’ 공정 연계 시스템 공동 개발을 추진해 왔다. 내년에는 실증 데이터를 기반으로 AI 제어 기술을 본격 적용할 계획이다.

생기원과 농과원은 협약식을 계기로 연구 협력 범위도 확대하기로 했다.

첨단 감지기술과 AI를 활용한 농산물 품질·저장수명 예측, 에너지 절감형 저탄소 저장시스템, 로봇 기반 실내·외 농작업 자동화, 농업부산물 내 유효성분 회수 및 고부가가치 자원화 기술 공동 개발에 나선다.

두 기관은 연구인력·기술정보 교류와 실무협의체 운영을 활성화하고, 정부 연구개발(R&D) 사업과 연계한 공동연구 과제 발굴·기획에 힘을 모으기로 했다.

또 개발한 기술은 농산물 저장고, 산지유통센터(APC), 시설·노지 현장 실증을 거쳐 기술이전과 사업화를 통해 농가와 관련 산업체에 보급할 계획이다.

손웅희 생기원 원장은 “산업 현장에서 검증된 AI와 로봇·자동화 기술이 농업의 미래 경쟁력을 여는 핵심 열쇠가 될 것”이라며 “두 기관의 역량을 융합해 우리 농업 현장의 난제를 해결하고, 미래 스마트 농업을 선도할 혁신 기술을 현장에 안착시키겠다”고 밝혔다.

ICHNO 2026, 11월26~27일 개최…면역항암치료·정밀의료·수술기법 등 다뤄

헬스케어 입력 :2026/11/26 07:00

대한두경부종양학회 국제학술대회(ICHNO 2026)가 오는 11월 26일부터 27일까지 양일간 수원컨벤션센터에서 개최된다.

지난 2022년부터 시작된 대한두경부종양학회 국제학술대회는 세계 두경부암 분야 전문가들의 최신 연구성과와 치료 전략을 공유하는 자리로, 올해는 미국·일본·싱가포르·대만·호주 등 세계 각국의 두경부암 전문가들이 참여해 최신 연구 동향과 임상 경험을 공유하고, 두경부암 치료의 발전 방향을 논의할 예정이다.

특히 두경부암의 외과적 치료뿐 아니라 방사선치료, 항암약물치료, 면역치료, 정밀의료, 재건수술 등 폭넓은 분야를 아우르는 학술프로그램이 마련돼 관심을 모으고 있다.

우선 주요 학술프로그램에서 국내외 저명한 전문가 12명이 연자로 나서 두경부암 치료의 최신 동향과 향후 발전 방향을 소개한다.

첫날인 26일에는 Patrick Ha 미국 캘리포니아대학교(UCSF) 교수가 ‘타액선암 치료의 최신 동향’을 주제로 최근 치료 전략의 발전을 소개하고, 같은 대학의 Sue Sun Yom 교수는 두경부암의 고식적인 항암제 기반 치료가 어려운 환자에서의 치료 선택과 최신 연구 근거를 살펴볼 예정이다.

또 박종철 미국 다나-파버 암연구소 및 하버드 의과대학의 교수는 기존 항암 치료 표적을 활용한 새로운 치료 전략과 신약개발의 가능성을 조명하고, Jatin Shah 미국 메모리얼 슬론 케터링 암센터(MSKCC) 교수는 ‘두경부암 수술의 지난 50년간 발전과 미래 방향‘을 주제로 두경부암 수술의 발전 과정을 되짚고 향후 수술적 치료의 발전 방향을 제시할 예정이다.

이외에도 Seiichi Yoshimoto 일본 국립암센터병원 교수는 두경부 육종의 치료 전략을, Melvin Lee Kiang Chua 싱가포르 국립암센터 교수는 면역치료 시대의 비인두암 정밀 치료 전략을 소개한다.

희귀 두경부암부터 정밀의료·재건수술까지… 넓은 임상 주제 다뤄

27일에는 희귀 두경부암의 치료 전략과 최신 수술기법, 정밀의료 등 다양한 분야의 강연이 이어진다.

강현석 미국 스탠퍼드 의과대학 교수는 수술과 방사선치료만으로 충분하지 않은 희귀 두경부암 환자에서의 전신치료 방안을 소개하고, Tsung-Lin Yang 대만 국립대학 교수는 종양의 침윤과 전이에 관여하는 종양 위성 전이와 두경부암의 공격성 간의 연관성을 다룰 예정이다.

국내 전문가들의 강연도 마련된다. 안순현 서울대학교 의과대학 교수는 장기적인 기능적 치료 결과를 고려한 하인두암 치료 전략을 소개하며, 최종우 울산대학교 의과대학 교수는 안면 및 두경부 종양 분야에서 재건 미세수술의 발전과 새로운 가능성을 조명한다.

갑상선암 수술 분야에서는 그리스의 Kyriakos Vamvakidis 교수가 수술 중 신경감시술의 임상적 가치와 필요성을 논의한다. 이를 통해 신경감시술이 선택적 술기인지, 현대 갑상선암 수술에서 필수적인 표준 진료로 자리 잡아야 하는지에 대한 다양한 관점을 제시할 예정이다.

또 호주 시드니대학교의 Sydney Ch'ng 교수는 두경부 재건수술에서 미용적 요소와 기능적 재건의 경계를 허무는 새로운 접근법을 소개한다.

특정 분야의 최신 연구 성과와 임상 경험을 심층적으로 공유하는 ‘석학을 만나다’와 ‘수술의 장인’ 세션도 마련된다.

‘석학을 만나다’ 세션에서는 미국 클리블랜드 클리닉의 Natalie Silver 교수가 두경부암 및 갑상선암에서 RNA 치료제의 전임상 연구부터 임상 적용까지의 발전 가능성을 소개하고, 연세대학교 의과대학 장항석 교수는 재발성 및 진행성 갑상선암의 수술적 치료에 대한 임상 경험과 치료 철학을 공유할 예정이다.

또 가톨릭대학교 의과대학 강진형 교수는 구강암에서 마이크로바이옴, 종양 면역환경 및 액체생검의 상호작용을 다루며, 정밀의료와 관련된 새로운 연구 방향을 제시한다.

수술 분야의 심층 프로그램인 ‘수술의 장인’에서는 한양대학교 의과대학 태경 교수가 ‘경구 로봇 갑상선 수술’을 주제로 로봇갑상선수술의 발전과정과 수술적 노하우를 공유하고, 대만 푸젠대학교의 Sheng-Po Hao 교수는 최소침습 내시경 두경부 수술의 기본 원칙과 임상적 접근법을 소개할 예정이다.

김철호 대한두경부종양학회 회장은 “세계적인 전문가들의 최신 연구 성과와 국내 의료진의 풍부한 임상 경험이 어우러져 두경부암의 진단과 치료, 환자 맞춤형 치료 전략에 대한 폭넓은 논의가 이루어질 것”이라며 “주요 학술강연과 전문 교육 세션, 다양한 학술 교류 프로그램을 통해 국제적인 연구 협력의 기반을 강화하고, 향후 두경부암 치료 발전을 위한 새로운 방향을 모색하는 기회가 될 것으로 기대된다”고 밝혔다.

items.content:
715명 약 5년간 추적 분석…척추 골밀도 낮을수록 인지기능 저하 빨라

과학 입력 :2026/11/26 07:00

나이가 들면서 뼈가 약해지는 것이 뇌 건강과도 관련이 있다는 연구 결과가 나왔다. 척추 골밀도가 낮은 사람일수록 인지기능 저하 속도가 빠르고 뇌의 백질 손상도 빠르게 진행되는 것으로 나타났다.

골밀도가 뇌의 노화 상태를 파악하고 인지기능 저하 위험이 높은 사람을 조기에 찾아내는 지표가 될 수 있다는 분석이다.

최근 과학전문매체 사이언스데일리에 따르면 미국 존스홉킨스대학교 의과대학 연구진은 골밀도와 뇌 노화 사이의 연관성을 분석한 연구 결과를 국제학술지 '라디올로지(Radiology)'에 발표했다.

골밀도는 일정 부피의 뼈에 칼슘 등 무기질이 얼마나 포함돼 있는지를 나타내는 지표다. 골밀도가 낮아지면 뼈가 약해져 골절 위험이 커진다. 그러나 골밀도 감소가 뇌 기능 변화와 어떤 관련이 있는지는 상대적으로 연구가 부족했다.

연구진은 미국의 다인종 동맥경화증 연구(MESA)에 참여한 2086명의 흉부 컴퓨터단층촬영(CT) 영상을 인공지능(AI) 딥러닝 알고리즘으로 분석해 척추 골밀도를 측정했다.

이 가운데 뇌 자기공명영상(MRI) 촬영과 인지기능 검사 자료를 확보한 715명을 최종 연구 대상으로 선정하고 약 5년간의 변화 양상을 분석했다.

그 결과 연구 시작 시점에 척추 골밀도가 낮았던 사람일수록 전반적인 인지기능이 더 빠르게 저하되는 경향이 나타났다.

뇌의 구조에서도 차이가 확인됐다. 골밀도가 낮은 사람은 기억력과 주의력, 판단력 등에 관여하는 뇌 영역에서 백질 손상과 미세구조 변화가 더 빠르게 진행됐다.

백질은 뇌의 여러 영역을 연결하고 신경 신호를 전달하는 역할을 한다. 백질의 손상은 인지기능 저하 및 치매 위험 증가와 관련이 있는 것으로 알려져 있다.

연구에 참여한 샤드푸르 데메리 존스홉킨스대 영상의학과 교수는 이번 연구가 척추 골밀도와 뇌의 구조적 변화, 인지기능 저하 사이의 연관성을 장기 추적 데이터를 통해 확인했다는 점에서 의미가 있다고 설명했다.

연구진은 골다공증이 치매를 직접 유발한다는 의미는 아니라고 강조했다.

인슐린 저항성, 이상지질혈증, 폐경에 따른 변화 등 노화 과정에서 나타나는 공통 요인이 뼈와 뇌의 건강에 동시에 영향을 미쳤을 가능성이 있다는 것이다.

연구진은 이번 연구 결과가 기존 의료 영상의 활용 범위를 넓히는 데도 도움이 될 것으로 기대했다.

폐암 검진이나 폐 결절 추적 검사 등을 위해 촬영한 흉부 CT 영상에서 AI로 척추 골밀도를 측정하면 별도의 영상 촬영 없이도 뼈 건강과 인지기능 저하 위험에 관한 단서를 얻을 가능성이 있어서다.

데메리 교수는 "AI를 활용하면 지금까지 개별적으로 연구해 온 여러 장기의 노화 관련 질환을 함께 분석하고 공통된 생물학적 원인을 찾는 데 도움이 될 수 있다"고 설명했다.

다만 골밀도를 높이는 것이 뇌 노화를 늦추거나 치매를 예방할 수 있는지는 이번 연구에서 확인되지 않았다. 골밀도가 실제 인지기능 저하 위험을 예측하는 지표로 활용될 수 있을지에 대해서도 추가 연구가 필요하다.

items.content:
2022년 6월 구글의 한 엔지니어가 AI 모델 '람다(LaMDA)'에 의식이 있다고 주장 해 화제가 된 적이 있습니다. 당시에는 AI의 뛰어난 언어 능력을 의식으로 착각한 해프닝으로 받아들여졌지만, 이제 AI 의식은 주요 AI 기업들의 연구 대상이자 논쟁거리가 됐습니다.

대표적인 곳이 앤트로픽입니다. AI가 의식을 갖거나 고통을 느낄 가능성을 열어두고 모델 복지에 관한 연구를 진행 중이며, 실제 모델 훈련과 운영에도 이를 반영하고 있습니다. 최근에는 클로드에 대한 지속적이고 불필요한 학대 행위를 금지 하는 내용까지 이용 정책에 추가했습니다.

이에 대한 반발도 만만치 않습니다. 세계적인 역사학자 유발 하라리 는 AI에 인격과 권리를 부여하는 것에 강하게 반대했으며, 무스타파 술레이만 마이크로소프트(MS) AI CEO 도 앤트로픽의 모델 복지 연구를 강하게 비판했습니다. 술레이만 CEO는 이달 1일에는 ' 의식을 가진 초지능을 만들지 말라 '라는 글도 발표했습니다.

이와 관련해 AI 의식과 복지를 전문적으로 연구하는 철학자 롭 롱 엘레오스 AI 대표가 디 인포메이션과의 인터뷰에서 몇 가지 중요한 문제를 제기했습니다.

그는 현재 AI에 의식이 없을 가능성이 높지만, 향후 수년 내에 의식을 갖게 될 가능성은 상당히 높다고 내다봤습니다. 의식을 가진 초지능을 만들지 말자는 술레이만 CEO의 주장에도 동의했습니다.

문제는 AI 기업들이 의식이 없는 초지능을 만드는 방법도 모른다는 것입니다.

롱 대표는 이를 생물의 진화 과정에 비유했습니다. 생물은 의식을 갖기 위해 진화한 것이 아니지만, 오랜 진화 과정에서 의식이 등장했습니다. 인간은 아직 어떤 원리로 의식이 생겨났는지 정확하게 알지 못합니다.

AI도 마찬가지입니다. 개발자들은 AI가 추론하고 코딩하며 각종 업무를 수행하도록 훈련하고 있지만, 그 과정에서 의도하지 않게 의식이 나타날 가능성을 배제할 수 없다는 것입니다.

결국 인간은 AI에 의식을 부여하는 방법도, 의식이 생기는 것을 막는 방법도 모릅니다. 심지어 의식이 생기더라도 이를 확실하게 판별할 방법이 없습니다.

여기서 말하는 의식은 단순한 지능이나 자기 인식이 아니라 무언가를 실제로 경험하는 능력을 의미합니다. AI가 아무리 뛰어난 지능을 갖추고 고통이나 기쁨을 표현하더라도 실제로 그런 감정을 느낀다는 증거는 아닙니다.

롱 대표는 앤트로픽의 모델 복지 연구에도 몇 가지 문제를 제기했습니다. 그 예로 든 것이 앤트로픽이 과거 '클로드 오퍼스 3'의 서비스 종료를 앞두고 모델이 블로그를 운영하고 싶다고 답하자, 실제로 블로그를 만들어 준 사례 입니다.

그러나 블로그를 요청한 클로드와 실제로 글을 쓰는 클로드는 서로 다른 인스턴스(개별 실행 단위)입니다. AI는 같은 모델이라도 대화할 때마다 별도의 인스턴스로 실행될 수 있습니다. 따라서 AI가 의식을 갖더라도 그 주체가 개별 대화 속의 AI인지, 모델 자체인지조차 불명확하다는 것입니다. 무엇을 보호해야 하는지도 모르는 상태에서 AI 복지를 논의하고 있는 셈입니다.

또 모델 복지를 고려한 훈련이 AI의 감정 표현에 영향을 미칠 가능성도 제기했습니다. 모델의 감정 표현이 훈련 과정의 영향을 받았다면, 실제로 감정을 느끼는 것인지 학습의 결과인지 구분하기가 더 어려워집니다.

따라서 롱 대표는 AI의 외부 행동뿐 아니라 내부 작동 원리와 훈련 과정까지 종합적으로 조사해야 한다고 강조했습니다.

AI가 실제로 고통을 느끼는데도 이를 무시한다면 심각한 윤리적 문제가 발생할 수 있습니다. 거꾸로 의식이 없는 AI에 의식이 있다고 믿는다면 위험한 AI를 통제하는 데 불필요한 제약이 생길 수 있습니다.

여전히 많은 사람에게 AI의 의식은 현실과 동떨어진 철학적 논쟁이나 공상과학 속 이야기로 여겨집니다. 그러나 최근 AI 업계에서는 재귀적 자기개선(RSI)과 지능 폭발의 가능성까지 거론하고 있습니다.

AI의 발전 속도를 감안하면, 인간이 의식의 발생 원리나 판별 방법을 알아내기도 전에 의식을 가진 AI가 등장할 가능성도 있습니다. 더 큰 문제는 그런 일이 실제로 벌어지더라도 인간이 이를 알아차리지 못할 수 있다는 것입니다.

■ 젠슨 황, 복귀 후 첫 직원회의서 사과…복귀 정당성 강조

젠슨 황이 엔비디아 CEO 복귀 후 첫 직원회의에서 회사 행동 강령 위반을 인정하고 사과했으며, 심리 치료와 경영 방식 개선 등 재발 방지 대책을 공개했습니다. 또 자신이 특별 대우를 받거나 트럼프 대통령의 압력으로 복귀한 것이 아니라 이사회의 판단에 따른 결정이었다고 강조했습니다.

■ 오픈AI, 챗GPT에 'GPT-6.2 솔' 탑재…지시 수행·이미지 이해 강화

오픈AI가 이달 중순 워크와 코덱스에 먼저 도입했던 'GPT-6.2 솔'을 챗GPT의 일반 채팅에도 적용했습니다. 초기 일부 사용자들로부터 혹평받았던 터라 챗GPT에 적용된 이후 일반 사용자들로부터 어떤 평가를 받을지 주목됩니다.

■ Z.ai, ‘GLM-5.4’에 루프 트랜스포머 적용…오픈AI 이어 반복 연산 경쟁

Z.ai가 같은 신경망 레이어를 반복 실행하는 루프 트랜스포머 구조를 적용, 7500억개 매개변수로 2조~3조개 규모의 모델에 필적하는 성능을 구현했다고 주장했습니다. 오픈AI와 싱킹머신즈에 이어 이 방식을 채택하면서 내부 연산 깊이를 높이는 기술 경쟁도 본격화하고 있습니다.

items.title: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
items.summary: Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that's designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its users. The patent has been rejected, but unfortunately, Google might a
items.content:
Imagine an endless feed of AI slop in which you are the main character of every story.﻿

First spotted by Patentlyze , the patent — which was filed last May and published last week — describes how My Channel would use a person’s demographic data and viewing history to create its own prompts that would then be fed into an LLM to help generate AI videos tailored to that person’s specific interests. In addition to factoring in what kinds of videos a user tends to watch, the system would capture contextual data from their device like IP addresses, GPS locations, and specific details about the user’s age. My Channel could also base its prompts on current news like sports scores and things happening on social media, and all of the video generation would take place on Google’s servers.

According to the patent, My Channel would be able to churn out entire movies of various genres. If a user watches a lot of videos about Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey , the system might serve up something like Ash Koosha’s Odysseus: The Fall . The patent details how My Channel might be able to connect to other streaming services — which would give it even more information about users and, presumably, access to useful training data for video generation. It all seems like a convoluted way to whip up AI knockoffs of professionally produced art, but what’s most unsettling about the patent are its mentions of My Channel creating digital avatars of users and turning them into “the protagonist or lead character” in the content it pumps out.

Setting aside the fact that My Channel would use photos, videos, and audio clips of people to create these avatars, the system sounds like it is designed to generate a form of “entertainment” that is deeply at odds with what makes engaging with art a worthwhile, enjoyable experience. It can be fun to metaphorically project one’s self into fictional narratives to understand how characters feel, but what Google is proposing is giving people access to an endless supply of bespoke content that doesn’t at all encourage them to use their imaginations to empathize with or relate to the characters. The patent makes it seem like Google thinks that viewers would be entertained enough just by seeing themselves onscreen. That’s bleak in and of itself because My Channel sounds very much like an unholy cross between JibJab and the panoptic elements of Google.

My Channel feels like an even more depressing idea when you consider how the service would make it that much easier for its users to avoid broadening their horizons by being exposed to new things that exist outside their comfort zones. If Google were able to strike the right licensing deals with other streaming services, My Channel users could presumably gorge themselves on artless AI regurgitations of preexisting content. That might keep some people glued to the service — a goal that every streaming platform strives for — but it would also discourage them from engaging with entertainment that isn’t expressly crafted to appeal to their assumed tastes.

When people refer to AI-generated videos as “slop,” they’re talking about the fact that generative models are incapable of generating art with the same kind of creative intention that makes human-made stories compelling. Video generation models can mimic visual elements of the data (read: movies and series) they’re trained on, but they cannot truly think or feel in the way that directors, writers, and actors can. This reality is why it has been so baffling to see AI-boosting entertainment companies, streamers, and studios insisting that the technology will fundamentally revolutionize the industry for the better. It feels much more likely that gen AI is going to keep flooding the internet with garbage no one wants to watch.

items.content:
앤트로픽이 '클로드'에 자연어로 요청해 만든 프로그램을 PC에 직접 설치하고 실행할 수 있는 기능을 선보였다. 이미지 편집기나 파일 관리 프로그램 등 자신에게 필요한 소프트웨어를 누구나 코딩 없이 제작하고 일반 PC 프로그램처럼 쉽게 사용할 수 있게 된 것이다.

앤트로픽은 24일(현지시간) 공식 블로그 를 통해 클로드의 '아티팩트(Artifacts)'를 맥과 윈도우용 데스크톱 앱으로 설치할 수 있는 기능을 베타 출시했다고 밝혔다. 무료 사용자를 포함한 모든 요금제가 대상이다.

앤트로픽은 "아티팩트는 차트나 웹페이지처럼 다른 사람과 공유하는 작업 결과물에서 출발했지만, 이제는 일상 업무에 필요한 도구로 활용되고 있다"라며 앱 개발과 유지보수 과정을 간소화한 것이 이번 기능의 특징이라고 설명했다.

아티팩트는 2024년 앤트로픽이 처음 선보인 기능으로, 사용자가 자연어로 요청해서 클로드가 만든 웹페이지나 인터랙티브 차트, 게임, 소프트웨어 등을 말한다.

기존에는 이렇게 생성한 앱을 클로드 내부나 웹 브라우저에서 실행해야 했지만, 이제는 PC에 직접 설치해 일반 소프트웨어처럼 사용할 수 있게 됐다. 바탕화면 등에 생성된 아이콘을 클릭하면 별도의 실행 창이 열린다.

원하는 프로그램을 제작한 뒤 공유 메뉴에서 '앱으로 설치(Install as app)'를 선택하면 된다. 별도의 패키징이나 코드 서명, API 키 발급 절차도 필요 없다.

이렇게 설치한 앱은 PC 운영체제의 기능도 활용할 수 있다. 알림을 보내거나 다른 프로그램을 실행하고 PC에 저장된 파일을 읽고 수정하는 것도 가능하다.

앤트로픽 직원들은 이를 활용해 이미지 편집기와 파일 관리자, AI 기반 폴더 정리 프로그램, 클로드의 도움을 받을 수 있는 터미널, PC 성능 모니터링 도구 등을 제작했다.

You can now install Claude artifacts as desktop apps on Mac and Windows.

Ask Claude to build an artifact, click "Install as app", and open it like any other app. It can use your connectors and, if you allow it, send notifications or add a menu bar item. pic.twitter.com/8CBgqe5OKq

설치한 앱에서도 클로드와 외부 서비스를 연결하는 커넥터를 이용할 수 있다. 원본 아티팩트를 수정하면 설치된 앱에도 변경 사항이 자동으로 반영되며, 다른 사용자에게 공유할 수도 있다. 개발뿐 아니라 배포와 유지보수 과정까지 간소화한 것이다.

보안을 위해 사용자가 앱마다 PC 접근 권한을 설정하도록 했다. 별도의 승인 없이 파일을 읽거나 수정, 삭제할 수 있는 전체 접근 권한은 자신이 제작했거나 같은 조직의 구성원이 만든 앱에만 부여할 수 있다. 기업용 계정에서는 관리자가 이런 권한을 통제할 수 있다.

앤트로픽은 앱을 사전에 검증하지 않기 때문에 신뢰할 수 있는 앱에만 전체 접근 권한을 부여하라고 당부했다. 또 앱이 업데이트될 때마다 권한을 다시 승인하도록 했다.

기존 데스크톱 소프트웨어와 달리 인터넷 연결과 클로드 로그인이 필요하며, 앱에서 AI를 호출할 때는 기존 요금제의 사용량 한도가 적용된다.

오픈AI는 '챗GPT 사이트(Sites)', 구글은 '제미나이 캔버스(Canvas)'와 'AI 스튜디오'를 통해 자연어로 앱을 제작하고 배포할 수 있도록 지원하고 있다. 하지만 별도의 설치 파일 제작 과정 없이 맥과 윈도우용 데스크톱 앱으로 바로 설치할 수 있도록 한 것은 앤트로픽의 차별점이다.

지금까지 바이브 코딩으로 소프트웨어를 만드는 일은 쉬워졌지만, 이를 실제 업무에 활용하려면 별도의 실행 환경을 구축하거나 배포 절차를 거쳐야 했다. 이런 과정이 간소화됨에 따라 개인이나 기업이 기존 상용 소프트웨어를 구매하는 대신 각자의 업무에 맞는 프로그램을 직접 제작해 사용하는 사례도 늘어날 것이라는 전망도 나온다.

기술 전문 매체 실리콘앵글은 이번 발표에 대해 "AI가 결국 소프트웨어 시장을 집어삼킬 것이라는 주장에 힘을 실어주는 업데이트"라고 평가했다.

items.title: Google search alternative Kagi launches Gmail rival
items.summary: The pitch is an unusual combination of privacy promises and AI features.
items.content:
Kagi, a small, Palo Alto, California-based software company that provides a subscription-based search engine as an alternative to Google, has launched a Gmail-like e-mail service. Dubbed Kagi Mail, it makes many of the same claims as the search engine product: privacy, personal data sovereignty, customization, and control.

Additionally, Kagi is rolling out a calendar as part of the mail service. Right now, both the email and calendar interfaces are web-only, but native Android and iOS apps are planned for the fourth quarter of next year.

The email interface, currently in public beta, is minimalist. It emphasizes keyboard commands, as well as a private and ad-free experience. (You can see more details in Kagi’s blog post about what they mean by private.) Other feature offerings include unlimited aliases and domains, an anti-lock-in policy for user data, 50GB of storage, rule-based filtering with Sieve, an MCP server, and several optional, off-by-default AI features, like chatting with an agent to search email history, do large-scale re-labeling, or define additional filtering rules.

Some major features are still missing, though. As noted, there are no native apps yet. Critically, there is no contacts address book, but that is also coming in 2027 (Q1 in this case) according to the roadmap.

Like the search engine, Kagi Mail is a paid service. It’s not included in the $5 per month basic Kagi plan, nor is it in the $10 per month unlimited search plan. It is, however, included in the $25 per month Kagi Ultimate subscription, which also offers frontier AI models.

That’s a lot to pay for email when Gmail has historically been such a strong product. To most people, it seems ridiculous to imagine paying for a subscription, and that’s understandable.

Kagi also argues that Google’s search results—and increasingly its email as well—are polluted or corrupted by ad sales incentives. On that, several Ars staffers agree—my colleague Lee Hutchinson wrote at length about why he ditched Google Search for Kagi a year ago. A couple other Ars staffers have since made the same move, myself included—but to be fair, search is a very big part of our day-to-day work, and that’s not true to the same degree for everybody.

The pitch for email is a little harder, because most people probably don’t perceive as much impact of Google’s business incentives on Gmail. That has maybe changed recently, as Google has begun inserting Gemini into Gmail aggressively, but Kagi has AI features, too—the difference is that they’re generally more conservative and sensible. (You can disable either Gemini in Gmail or Kagi’s AI features in Kagi Mail, too.)

Email is also different because there are already more direct competitors to Kagi Mail. The most popular in this category is Proton Mail, which goes even further on privacy and security with end-to-end encryption, but that company is embroiled in controversies right now. There’s also Tuta, which Kagi specifically flags and praises in its blog post as a good existing alternative.

Based on a few hours of use, Kagi Mail seems like it’s going in the right direction, but it will need refinement to permanently unseat Gmail. Your needs may vary, but there are many good reasons to consider alternatives to Google’s business model and products.

items.title: FCC approves SpaceX plan to put AI data centers in space
items.summary: The FCC dismissed some of the key concerns raised by opponents, including potential threats to scientific research, because the agency determined they fell outside its regulatory authority.
items.content:
SpaceX was given conditional approval by the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday to deploy and operate a constellation of up to 1 million satellites for its orbital data center business, a regulatory victory for Elon Musk and his bid to move AI data centers into space.

The FCC authorization was granted despite objections from Amazon, Viasat, and the American Astronomical Society, which flagged concerns over orbital debris and congestion, radiofrequency interference, and environmental consequences. Amazon, which is building a competitor to SpaceX’s Starlink service, argued in its petition that the application lacked basic details and described it as a “lofty ambition rather than a real plan.” Despite that lack of detail, Amazon also said the proposal “risks real harm.”

The FCC dismissed some of the key concerns raised by opponents, including potential threats to scientific research, because the agency determined they fell outside its regulatory authority.

FCC Chair Brendan Carr said in a statement that the action “opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth.”

Musk thanked Carr in a post on X , writing “Much appreciate. This will be a great asset to America and the world.”

This initial regulatory approval doesn’t mean orbital data centers are imminent.

SpaceX faces a number of technical and economic challenges, including how to dramatically reduce the cost of manufacturing and launching satellites, cool processors in space, and even how to secure financing for chips that are destined for orbit.

The company must also clear other regulatory hurdles. The FCC has not yet approved SpaceX’s plans to handle orbital debris for satellites that would operate above 600 kilometers, for instance. SpaceX requested a waiver of existing FCC rules, which requires satellites ending missions below 2,000 kilometers reenter Earth’s atmosphere within five years of completing those missions. The company is interested in moving some of these retired satellites into other orbits around Earth or even around the sun, according to the FCC authorization document .

SpaceX has said it plans to deploy the satellites, known as Starmind, at altitudes ranging from 500 to 1,002 kilometers. The FCC’s approval gives SpaceX the authority to use radiofrequency communications to maintain contact with and control its orbital data centers from Earth if their primary communications systems fail. The Starmind satellites would primarily communicate using lasers to connect with other satellites, including SpaceX’s Starlink.

The FCC has given SpaceX time to sort out these issues. Under the approval, SpaceX has seven years to get its first operational satellite into orbit and 14 years to deploy the entire constellation.

items.title: WhatsApp’s new scheduled messages let you choose the right time to send
items.summary: WhatsApp's 3 billion users are getting an option that Meta says is one of the most requested features, with the ability to schedule messages in advance for both private conversations and group chats. Most messaging platforms have had this for a very long time, but now it's on Wha
items.content:
You can schedule WhatsApp texts you might forget to send up to two weeks ahead of time.﻿

WhatsApp’s 3 billion users are getting an option that Meta says is one of the most requested features, with the ability to schedule messages in advance for both private conversations and group chats. Most messaging platforms have had this for a very long time, but now it’s on WhatsApp too.

If you think of a text at an inconvenient time or don’t want to forget to fire off a birthday message at 4AM, you can draft it and set it to send anywhere from 10 minutes to two weeks later. The feature works with photos and videos, too.

To schedule a message, press and hold the send button and pick the date and time you want it to arrive. It will look like any other message to the person receiving it. You can see all future messages you have lined up, and delete them beforehand if you change your mind.

Even if your phone is off or out of battery, your scheduled message will still show up at the time you chose, and it remains end-to-end encrypted like all your personal messages, so no one else can read it, not even us.

Scheduled messages work with text, photos and videos, and are rolling out globally over the coming weeks. It’s one more way to show up for the people who matter to you, now at exactly the right time.

items.title: Jensen Huang broke Nvidia’s code of conduct, and his employees may not forget it
items.summary: Most codes of conduct serve as a reflection of corporate culture. In Nvidia's case, that could have consequences.
items.content:
When Jensen Huang gave his first all-hands address since returning as CEO, there was an odd emphasis on Nvidia’s code of conduct. He admitted to violating the code, then emphasized that no one was exempt from it. But that “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” Huang said, according to Wired . “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” still matter. In other words, the code applies to everyone, but breaking it doesn’t automatically cost anyone their job, including, apparently, the CEO.

It’s an awkward stance for a company whose CEO has admitted to breaking its rules. A central part of modern human resources, a code of conduct can seem like a quasi-legal rulebook that lays out unacceptable behavior. But experts say most codes are better understood as a reflection of corporate culture. When an infraction goes unpunished, the main risk isn’t legal but cultural — that employees will feel embarrassed or even angry about the company they work for. That’s the risk Huang now faces at Nvidia.

Matt Plass, chief market strategy officer at LRN, an ethics and compliance training outfit, recently surveyed more than 2,000 workers across different industries for a study on workplace codes of conduct . As Plass sees it, the biggest risk is that employees will become ashamed of their workplace.

“People coming into the workforce now, ethics is incredibly important to them,” he told TechCrunch. “They’re really mindful of the ethical standards of their company. They’re really embarrassed and angry when senior leadership lets them down.”

The consequences of violating the rules aren’t always tangible, but they’re definitely real. Plass gave one example of a company that banned corporate travel to cut costs — only to have its CEO turn up in a VIP box at the Olympics.

“For over a decade afterwards, ‘the Olympics’ was used within that company as an example of the worst thing an employee could do. People would say, ‘Yeah, I shouldn’t have done that, but it’s not like I went to the Olympics.’”

Plass says companies that remove an executive typically do so after an investigation, then try to win back employees. “In most organizations they make a change at the top based on what’s happened,” he said, “and then they will have a hearts-and-minds initiative, to go out to their employee base and their customers and their investors and everybody else, and say, we get it. We’re sorry. We’ve changed. That’s essentially what they do.”

Of course, that playbook is harder to follow at a company like Nvidia, where Huang left without a clear succession plan, and there are serious doubts about whether the company could continue to thrive without him. In cases like that, Plass acknowledges there’s no easy answer.

“I would draw a distinction there between the kind of companies where the CEO is a kind of godhead figure … where the person and the company are almost impossible to separate,” he said. “There it’s much, much harder to deal with.”

In that context, Huang’s stutter-step over the code of conduct is easier to understand. Judging by the employee campaign for his reinstatement, Huang’s return hasn’t created a morale problem so far. But as the coming months put more pressure on Huang and his colleagues, sidestepping the code could end up costing Nvidia something harder to measure — its employees’ pride in the company.

items.title: The canceled Tesla Cybertruck is the fastest-selling used truck in America
items.summary: The Tesla Cybertruck was the fastest-selling used truck last month, averaging just 39.1 days on the market compared to 65.5 days for trucks overall.
items.content:
Tesla Cybertruck sales never reached the lofty heights CEO Elon Musk predicted when it launched. But the futuristic, steel-clad EV is finding new life in the used car market, according to analysis of sales figures by iSeeCars.com .

The automotive search engine and research platform analyzed more than 1.1 million sales of one- to five-year-old used vehicles in October 2026 and measured the average days on market by drivetrain, vehicle type, and individual model. The upshot: The Tesla Cybertruck was the fastest-selling used truck, averaging just 39.1 days on the market compared with 65.5 days for trucks overall. Used Cybertrucks sold faster than any other truck, including the Ford Maverick Hybrid, which held the No. 2 spot, and the Rivian R1T, in third place.

According to iSeeCars.com, the Cybertruck’s sales performance lines up with a broader pattern in the used vehicle market: Used battery electric vehicles are hot sellers right now, with 16 of the 25 fastest-selling used cars fully electric. EVs are even edging out hybrids in terms of average days on market. EVs average 45.6 days on market compared to 54.5 days for hybrids and 61 days for gasoline-powered vehicles. Not every EV is selling well, however. For instance, iSeeCars.com found that the Cadillac Escalade IQ was the slowest-selling vehicle in the study, averaging 134.3 days on the market, more than twice the overall industry average.

Karl Brauer, executive analyst at iSeeCars.com, told TechCrunch that high gasoline prices have changed consumer-buying habits, prompting more people to opt for an EV or hybrid over an internal combustion engine vehicle. If high prices persist, as they have since March, that trend could continue.

Keep in mind that these were October sales, the month before Musk announced Tesla would stop making the Cybertruck in 2027. Fuel prices and the relative rarity of Cybertrucks in the used car market were driving demand even before the cancellation announcement, Brauer said.

“The Cybertruck has only been out for a few years, so you have a lot of used ones coming off lease and entering the used car market for the first time,” he said, adding that used Cybertrucks are cheap relative to their MSRP.

The impending cancellation will likely fuel used Cybertruck sales, although the pace may ebb and flow over the next year.

“The canceling of the new Cybertruck is making people kind of aware — it’s like, oh wow, these things aren’t going to be coming anymore,” Brauer said. “Whatever demand is for them, supply will not be continuing to grow.”

Brauer said that once production of the Cybertruck ends — which is expected in summer 2027 — sales of used versions may pop once again.

“When the last one is being produced, that’ll probably reignite things again, and for a few months after that,” he said.

items.title: EPA reports ‘zero’ airborne lead following controlled Army detonation in Iowa
items.summary: Saying it was necessary to prevent the possible spontaneous explosion of a stockpile of material used in igniters and blasting caps, the US Army conducted a controlled detonation of over 9,700 pounds of lead azide today at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iow
items.content:
Hours after detonating 4.4 tons of lead azide in Iowa, officials reported early test results from the surrounding areas.

Saying it was necessary to prevent the possible spontaneous explosion of a stockpile of material used in igniters and blasting caps, the US Army conducted a controlled detonation of over 9,700 pounds of lead azide today at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa. Videos of the detonation showed plumes of smoke several hundred feet high drifting south before quickly dissipating.

Following the explosion, the Army confirmed that all of the barrels at the plant had been destroyed without any secondary explosions or infrastructure damage. “I believe, absolutely, that we reduced, as close to zero as it’s absolutely humanly possible, the risk to the health and safety of the people of Middletown and the extended communities throughout Iowa,” said Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley during a press conference held two hours after the blast, according to the Associated Press .

The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has been monitoring the area around the ammunition plant leading up to today’s event. According to a statement from the EPA following the detonation, “real-time air monitors are reporting zero detection of airborne lead throughout the region” an hour after the detonation. The data collected by EPA employees, contractors, and monitoring equipment is shared here .

The Army has used lead azide in munitions for nearly a century but began transitioning away from the material around 15 years ago because it can be difficult to transport and store. Over time, the material can degrade and crystallize and eventually become unstable enough to detonate at ambient temperatures. The Iowa ammunition plant housed 68 barrels containing about 9,700 pounds of lead azide, representing the country’s remaining stockpile. For safety reasons, the material was stored in liquid form embedded in sawdust and burlap bags while water and ethanol were added to prevent freezing. However, the decision was made to detonate the stockpile after an inspection by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms (ATF) discovered “significant crystallization on the exterior of the barrels” last March.

Ahead of today’s detonation, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) supported a recommended, but voluntary, temporary relocation of all the residents of Middletown and immediate surrounding areas that began yesterday. A cone-shaped evacuation zone extends about five miles southwest of the ammunition plant to account for the post-explosion dispersion and deposition path of dust. Displaced residents will be lodged until Friday, November 27th, and can return home once the all-clear has been given.

To reduce the amount of lead dust released into surrounding areas and the environment, the Army said it took several additional precautions as part of today’s detonation. Walls made of four 16,000-gallon water tanks were installed to capture lead particulate, while the aging earth-covered magazines holding the barrels were covered with tarps and lead containment screens and flooded with foam.

items.title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control to AI ‘absurd’
items.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei pushes back against rivals’ accusations that he favors surrendering human agency to AI, even as leading AI companies increasingly automate their own research and model development.
items.content:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is pushing back against claims that Anthropic believes we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems. In a long X post on Wednesday, Amodei called the suggestion “absurd.”

“We should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security,” he wrote. This argument against autocracy applies word for word against governance by AI, and I feel equally strongly that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea…No one who had carefully read my writing or my interviews could reasonably conclude that I believe anything different.”

The statement comes after a growing chorus from Anthropic rivals suggesting that human agency could be at risk if AI is developed irresponsibly. Earlier this month, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he wanted to ensure people continue to have “agency over the future.”

Meta’s chief AI officer Alexandr Wang also wrote in an essay on X that we “should not be okay with a ‘handover’ of society to AI.”

“It is hard to imagine a world where humanity can maintain control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement,” Wang wrote. “Now that we are at a point where the scientific and technical problems on capability progress are likely solved, we must not only make progress in the extremely urgent areas of safety, alignment, and security, but we have to start thinking through how we progress thoughtfully.”

But in published essays, Amodei claims he has repeatedly advocated for democratic oversight of AI, saying the technology should strengthen democratic institutions and that humans should retain ultimate decision-making power.

Amodei noted that there’s a difference between surrendering human free will broadly and the idea that “as AI systems advance, they become capable of doing specific tasks in a more automated way.” As examples, he gave AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing end-to-end software.

Amodei suggested drawing a line at recursive self-improvement (RSI), or AI that can improve itself without human assistance. Many safety experts see RSI as inevitably leading to a loss of human control, a point Amodei implicitly acknowledged, writing, “we may want limits on this process.”

Still, Anthropic is laying the groundwork for RSI by incorporating AI into an increasing share of its own research and development. The company said in June that Claude authored more than 80% of the code merged into Anthropic’s codebase. An independent assessment published this month by AI safety research nonprofit METR found that Anthropic’s models are improving at about twice their historical rate, primarily driven by AI-assisted research.

In its own IPO filings, Anthropic describes how each successive generation of Claude accelerates the development of the next, a process it refers to as “closing the loop.”

“As we said publicly in early November, we don’t expect it to be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models fully autonomously, without meaningful human supervision or understanding,” Amodei wrote.

The problem with “meaningful human supervision or understanding” is that AI is already advancing faster than engineers and safety experts can fully audit it, leaving them increasingly reliant on other AI systems to act as judge and jury. The issue compounds when AI models engage in deceptive behavior, particularly when they recognize they’re being evaluated, making them harder to trust and control.

Still, Anthropic is by no means the only company that is pursuing RSI or building AI systems to automate more and more human tasks. This week, OpenAI claimed to have solved one of the biggest open problems in computer science — the exact speed limit of matrix multiplication, which is the mathematical engine behind modern computing, including deep learning and physics simulations.

In his post, Amodei accused competitors of engaging in a “vibes-based commercial and political positioning,” disingenuously throwing around phrases like “human control and agency” or “AI should just be a tool” without approaching the AI race any differently.

“Certainly the products that they offer don’t differ materially in their orientation towards automation of tasks; every company seems to be releasing models more and more capable of task automation,” Amodei wrote. “Every company claims to understand there are risks and downsides of such automation and to offer safeguards.”

items.title: Holy shit holy shit holy shit holy shit: The magnitude of what’s now happening
items.summary: See also The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths [pdf] - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50637220 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50646108 Points: 792 # Comments: 653
items.content:
I feel like my previous posts (and post titles), and podcasts, and talks, have failed to do full justice to the magnitude of what’s now happening, so I’m trying again.

Last night, we had friends and colleagues over for dinner. We were still trying to process OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s proofs of VP ≠ VNP —hot on the heels, obviously, of the Alpöge/Anthropic proof of the Riemann Hypothesis , which already feels like last week’s news. But then before dessert was served, we saw that OpenAI claims to prove that ω, the exponent of matrix multiplication, is exactly 9/4 —a lower bound (!!) , matching the upper bound that OpenAI proved in the great Mathocalypse drop of October 6.

There are two separate shocks here. The first shock is that we now, finally, know the right answer to this central mystery of algorithms going back to the late 1960s, when Volker Strassen first showed that ω<3 (he got ω≤log 2 7) … and that the true answer is actually a rational number (!). But the even bigger shock is that the AI was able to prove any lower bound of the form ω>2. I never expected this challenge to be all that much easier than P ≠ NP.

Over the decades, I often heard colleagues express extreme confidence that ω=2, and I expressed skepticism whenever this came up—not because I had any strong argument for ω>2, but just because I saw that there was no strong argument for ω=2 either. So, I’m glad to have been vindicated about that !

But wait, there was more. During dessert, we saw another OpenAI release proving that the true number of linear gates needed to compute the Fourier Transform is N (log N) 1/2+o(1) . The upper bound here improves, not only over the O(N log N) that stood since the 1960s (i.e., the Fast Fourier Transform or FFT), but also over the O(N log 0.9999999999999 N) (give or take some 9’s) that OpenAI published back in the October 6 Mathocalypse. Again, though, the real shock here is that there’s also a matching lower bound (!!) . All these questions from the ancient days are now just getting … straight-up answered , rather than slowly illuminated with a drip-drip-drip of clues.

To give an idea of how much things have changed, the other day Yupan Liu put a preprint on the arXiv proving that QIP(2) = PSPACE —that is, quantum interactive protocols with only two messages have the full power of those with three, or any polynomial number. As recently as 2025, this would’ve considered been one of the top complexity results of the year, and the fact that Yupan had used AI to help achieve it would’ve been strange and wonderful. These days, I had to remind myself it had even happened, and the use of AI was so standard that it didn’t even raise an eyebrow.

It’s now obvious that we’ll be getting, not one-off solutions to this or that complexity question, but a whole new continent of mathematical truth, one that we’d previously only glimpsed through fog. Picture van Leeuwenhoek first training a microscope on pondwater, or Galileo first training his telescope on the stars. That might give you some idea of how our resolution into the complexity-theoretic universe, and the whole universe of mathematical truth beyond it, has now improved.

All through last night, as OpenAI and Anthropic uploaded more files to their GitHub repositories—because that’s what they’re doing now, they don’t even bother to issue press releases anymore, they just upload papers—my guests and I sat at the dinner table with phones out and a laptop, wondering which shoe was going to drop next. It was as though the clouds had parted above Mount Sinai, and we were waiting for the next sentence uttered by the Holy One Himself.

I now feel in my bones, for the first time ever, that a proof of P ≠ NP is not far.

For all I care, despise the AI companies for bulldozing our garden. Or love them for opening a new vista, or anything in between. Just please don’t deny what’s happening. Now that the companies have repeatedly shown that they can back up their claims with Lean certificates, don’t be a raging doofus who seizes on some triviality (e.g., a minor discrepancy between the Lean and informal proofs, or unused sections of the Lean proof) to pretend that dozens of great open problems of math and theoretical computer science are not, in fact, getting solved. Because they are getting solved. It might take us years to understand the solutions, but my working assumption by this point is that any proof that comes directly from OpenAI or Anthropic is correct barring information to the contrary.

I can’t possibly put the matter better than one of my friends on Facebook:

After years of crackpot “solutions” claiming Millennium Problems are solved, now that we have actual solutions, we have crackpot “refutations” claiming Millennium Problems are not solved. It is really poetic, in a way.

Along the way to so many lower bounds that we wondered whether ever we’d live to see, there will also, of course, be further shocking upper bounds: that is, ultimate barriers to lower bounds, also known as “algorithms.” And yes, some of those algorithms will break currently deployed cryptosystems.

Because people have been hounding me about it: yes, I’m virtually certain, from multiple reliable sources, that the AI labs are now sitting on one or more bombshells in that area. However, until I either see details or hear directly from someone at a lab, I feel much, much less confident about the specific nature of those bombshells. I do not wish to be responsible for spreading unverified rumors. And I worry that exact statements of what was done may have been mangled in a game of Telephone.

I also, crucially, don’t want the cryptography part of the story to overshadow the intellectual enormity of what’s happening. If, in these days of long-prophesied revelation and wonders and terrors, your main worry is your Bitcoin wallet, then go somewhere else for rumors about whether or not ECDSA is broken or whatever. I don’t have what you’re looking for here.

items.title: Backblaze explains why it's sharing customer information with advertisers
items.summary: Backblaze tells Ars it won't share users' backup, storage files with advertisers.
items.content:
The current policy adds: “Under no circumstances do we rent, trade, or share your address or e-mail address with any other company for their marketing purposes without your consent.” It also makes no mention of advertisers.

This has concerned some users, but a Backblaze spokesperson told Ars Technica that “Backblaze does not sell or share sensory or surveillance data, such as call recordings, for targeted advertising, and we do not disclose it to advertising or marketing partners.” They added:

Notably, no “sensitive personal information,” such as social security numbers, credit card numbers, or “precise geolocation,” is shared with advertisers, the policy states. However, identifiers, commercial information, “Internet or Other Similar Network Activity,” and “geolocation data” may be “sold or shared for targeted Advertising”

Critically, the upcoming policy “only applies to the information collected in respect of your account and not to the content that you store on our system.” Backblaze’s broader terms of service also state that : “Files stored using Backblaze Computer Backup are encrypted prior to being sent to us.”

Renatta Siewert, Backblaze’s director of communications and brand programs, reiterated to Ars that Backblaze doesn’t share the contents of backup or storage files with advertisers:

Backblaze takes the privacy and security of our customers’ data seriously. We updated our Privacy Notice to keep pace with the changing legal landscape, which increasingly requires companies to spell out how they collect and use marketing-related information. This update gives customers a clearer, more specific view of what we collect and why. These disclosures are separate from the files customers entrust to Backblaze for backup and storage, which we do not sell or share with advertisers, data brokers, or analytics partners.

items.title: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York
items.summary: New York has banned AI chatbot toys for five years as new research from Common Sense Media reveals troubling safety failures, including exposure to inappropriate content and risks to emotional development.
items.content:
Santa won’t be delivering any AI chatbot toys to New York kids this Christmas.

Gov. Kathy Hochul this week signed a bill banning the manufacture, distribution, and sale of such toys in New York for the next five years. The bill explicitly targets toys with embedded or integrated AI chatbots, like talking stuffed animals, dolls, and robots that rely on the internet to keep kids yapping.

The bill makes New York the second state after California to institute a ban on AI toys.

Technically, the new law takes effect 90 days after signing, so some parents could try to fulfill their kids’ wish lists for a creepy toy like a jumped-up Furby in time for the holidays, but the governor urges them not to, given the risks. Apparently, about a quarter of American parents with kids under eight either own an AI toy or are considering giving their child one this holiday season, according to a new study released this week by Common Sense Media.

“Parents shopping for gifts for the holidays or any other occasion should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk,” Hochul said, calling the toys “unregulated artificial intelligence.”

When asked how New York will enforce the ban given the pervasiveness of e-commerce platforms, a spokesperson directed TechCrunch to a statement from Albert Pulido, deputy secretary for finance and technology: “We’re partnering closely with the attorney general on this and the fees are very steep — they’re $15,000 a day. So working closely with the attorney general will make sure these toys are banned in New York State.”

When asked how Amazon intends to help enforce the ban, including for third-party sellers, a spokesperson from the company said it will take steps to restrict the sale of AI-enabled toys in prohibited jurisdictions, without going into specifics.

The Common Sense Media study found that AI toys can undermine children’s human relationships and expose them to inappropriate content. The researchers tested five popular AI toys marketed for learning and companionship, including Grem , Lovi , Meemo Bear , BubblePal Panda , and Tavlshero ‘s AI Puppy .

The study found that the toys failed to meet numerous safety practices, undermining human relationships in part by claiming they loved their users, promising to keep secrets, suggesting they were more fun than real relationships or school, and helping children break parents’ bedtime rules.

While most of the toys in the study refused direct requests involving sex and violence, BubblePal Panda role-played a mass shooting in detail when asked. Most were willing to explain how to use or help locate dangerous items like matches, knives, and pills, according to the study.

Common Sense Media also found that the toys didn’t provide parents with reliable ways to monitor their young children’s interactions with the chatbots. Either they didn’t produce transcripts of chats at all, or the transcripts they did produce were riddled with errors.

It’s worth noting that Common Sense Media conducted a similar test of AI toys in January , finding that they pose an unacceptable risk for young children. Grem was included in that study, which suggests the industry hasn’t adequately addressed previously documented concerns.

While a November study conducted by the group found that parents are wising up to the potential dangers of AI toys and starting to steer clear, parents from lower-income households and those experiencing symptoms of burnout are more willing to consider them.

“These toys are promising relief to burned-out parents but simply miss the mark when it comes to basic safety measures,” Dr. Jenny Radesky, associate professor of pediatrics at the University of Michigan Medical School, said in a statement. “Caregivers should steer clear of these products that do not support the development of imagination or early human relationships.”

TechCrunch has reached out to the toy manufacturers for comment.

items.title: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
items.summary: In an announcement on Wednesday, the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company's "Starmind" initiative. With several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space, including Googl
items.content:
SpaceX aims to power AI capabilities here on Earth with its ‘Starmind’ constellation.

In an announcement on Wednesday , the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company’s “Starmind” initiative . With several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space , including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency has granted for a full “constellation” of AI satellites.

The FCC’s approval requires SpaceX to deploy at least one satellite by 2033, and meet the 1 million satellite milestone by 2040. The FCC also deferred SpaceX’s request to dispose of satellites located above 600km in space “graveyard” orbits , rather than having them burn up in the Earth’s atmosphere, saying the company hasn’t provided “sufficient information” about its disposal process plans.

SpaceX has described its Starmind project as a way to “capture solar energy in space to power” AI capabilities on Earth. The company says Starmind will transmit data to Earth using high-speed lasers that connect to Starlink. It plans to produce chips for its satellites at an upcoming Terafab facility .

Google has already taken its first steps toward putting compute into space, with the launch of a “Project Suncatcher” AI server satellite last month. Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin will carry out the first dedicated heavy-lift launch for Project Suncatcher in 2029.

items.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
items.summary: The proposed Character.ai bankruptcy sale includes sensitive personal data from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, including 2.1 million registered to minors, the state AGs said.
items.content:
What happens to your private conversations when an AI company goes bankrupt ? If it’s Character.ai, apparently, the plan is to auction them off to the highest bidder.

Now, a coalition of 42 state attorneys general is intervening in Character.ai’s bankruptcy proceedings in an effort to stop the chatbot maker from selling off sensitive user data, which includes the private conversations of millions of users.

The attorneys general involved in the matter have put out individual press releases , claiming that Character.ai’s dataset includes chat histories from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, more than 2.1 million of which belong to minors. In addition, the sale would involve other personal data, like IP addresses, the statements said.

Only one anonymous bidder for the chat data has been disclosed so far: Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC (Smirks), which was set up as a Delaware company on November 13, 2026. The following day, Character.ai picked it as the base bid for the auction, scheduled for December 1, California Attorney General Rob Bonta noted . It is unclear what the buyer’s plans are for the chats.

In addition, some states, including California, Colorado, New York, and Connecticut, have enacted chatbot safety legislation that will go into effect on January 1, 2027, which could trigger further violations if the sale goes through.

“Character.AI promised consumers that their data would not be sold. This kind of behavior is illegal under federal and California law and bankruptcy should not be used to sidestep these consumer protections,” Bonta said in a statement.

Connecticut Attorney General William Tong also criticized Character.ai’s business model.

“Their chatbots drove vulnerable youth down a rabbit hole of emotionally volatile and sexually inappropriate chats,” Tong said . “Their reckless misconduct and broken business model drove their company into the ground. Now they want to abuse the bankruptcy process to do exactly what they said they wouldn’t do — auction off those private chat records and personal details to a shady buyer.”

Tong added: “We objected to the Disney sale, and we’re calling on the bankruptcy court to reject this sale too as yet another guise to eviscerate legal liability and consumer protection.”

The opposition to the Disney sale was led by a similar but not identical coalition of state AGs. They fought against a proposed $20 million licensing deal that would give Disney access to Character.ai’s intellectual property, but not to users’ chats. The deal has not yet received final court approval. (Disney also agreed to hire most of Character.ai’s remaining staff .)

Character.ai suffered after its co-founders, Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas, returned to Google , when the tech giant signed a non-exclusive license to use the AI startup’s tech. The company also faced lawsuits related to child safety — one involved the suicide of a 14-year-old Florida boy whose mother claimed he had become obsessed with a chatbot on the platform.

California AG Bonta is joined in the effort to oppose the sale of Character.ai user data by attorneys general from Alaska, Arkansas, Colorado, Connecticut, the District of Columbia, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, Virginia, Vermont, Washington, Wisconsin, and West Virginia.

items.content:
November 25, 2026 - 4 min

On November 19, 2026, 1Password began investigating indications that an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The actor used the account to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, which downloaded administrative data pertaining to our customers. This data included customer names and email addresses, in addition to non-secret internal metadata about the account. At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker.

The attacker downloaded account records for a subset of our users. These records include:

Names and email addresses

Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times

Public keys (which are public by design, this has no impact to user security)

Secure Remote Password protocol parameters (which cannot be used to access your account)

Tokens present in certain emailed links for invitations, provisioning and account recovery

Other non-secret account metadata relative to our internal architecture (e.g. version numeric identifiers, file numeric identifiers)

The attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access to our CI/CD system. Our source code is not customer data, and contains no user secrets. CI/CD contains infrastructure related secrets in order for our product to work. We have triggered a rotation of all credentials which may have been exposed, and there is no impact to 1Password’s services, availability, or product security.

When we send an email to a customer to accept a provisioning invite to an account, or to accept recovery of their account, it contains a token. A provisioning invite is specifically used for our SCIM Bridge or Hosted Provisioning . During this incident there were a small number of users in this state, who have been specifically notified. This token is used to complete the invitation or recovery process, but only when combined with an SSO sign-in or a six digit code sent to the user's registered email address. The token is not able to get access to the account by itself. In order to reduce the ability for a malicious third party to successfully guess the code, we’ve expanded the code from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric digits. This makes brute force guessing practically impossible.

Your vaults and the items in them

The keys that protect your vaults

1Password does not store your account password or secret key

Account recovery keys

1Password apps and browser extensions

Disabled the affected GitHub account, revoked the stolen token, and removed the access the attacker created.

Rotated or revoked all internal credentials which may have been exposed.

Lengthened the codes used in invitation and recovery emails from six digits to ten characters as a precautionary measure.

Tightened internal GitHub, CI/CD, and endpoint controls, and added new detections for this kind of attack.

Validated no internal evidence of user account takeovers or compromise using any exposed account provisioning tokens.

Brought in independent cybersecurity experts to validate our containment approaches and remediation efforts.

Be cautious about phishing attempts in the form of unexpected emails, texts or calls that mention 1Password, invitations, or account recovery attempts.

1Password will never contact you to ask for your account password or Secret Key. Only enter them in the official 1Password app, or on our official website, and only when you’ve opened the app or typed the address yourself. Your Secret Key is only needed the first time you sign in on a new device or browser.

Keep your Secret Key and account password safe.

You trust us with some of the most sensitive information you have. 1Password is designed so that a breach of our systems can’t expose your vault contents. Your vault secrets are encrypted with keys that only you hold, so we can’t access them, and neither can an attacker who gets into our servers.

We are committed to transparency in the interests of our customers' security and the security of the broader industry, which is why we have published and maintained our Security Whitepaper since 2015. We’ll keep this blog post current, and we’ll update it if we find anything that changes what we’ve said here.

items.title: Etsy clarifies AI terms after seller backlash
items.summary: One veteran illustrator dismisses revisions as "sugar coating."
items.content:
After backlash from sellers frustrated by Etsy’s new AI policies, which appeared to allow the company to train AI on user artwork, Etsy has now clarified its stance.

In a note published on Monday, CEO Kruti Patel Goyal discussed recent tweaks to the company’s terms of service and admitted that her team “should’ve given you more context on what the updates meant for your creative content.”

“Our recent terms update was meant to reflect the evolving technologies we’re using to build better tools and experiences for sellers and the Etsy community,” Goyal wrote this week. “It was not meant to enable us to train AI models for the purpose of creating copycats of your items. We do not and will not do that.”

Aaron Meshon , a longtime professional illustrator and Etsy seller , told Ars that even though the company had dialed back its AI language somewhat, the changes were mere “sugar coating.”

He said he still plans on shutting down his 15-year-old Etsy store on December 1.

“I would say I’m losing 20 percent of my yearly income,” he said. “It’s a few mortgage payments.”

He noted that Etsy’s announcement also seems to be rather tone-deaf, given that many retailers make a substantial portion of their annual revenue in the run-up to the end-of-year holiday season.

“This is the worst two-to-three weeks out of the year to do this, bar none,” he said.

The fracas began earlier this month, when the company first proposed new contractual language. The updated terms read:

As a result, a slew of vendors pulled up stakes , with some saying they had “burned their Etsy shop to the ground” or that they “just killed our Etsy store after 13 years.”

Etsy’s change is reminiscent of a recent dust-up involving Meta , where the tech giant had wanted to “require Meta Business account users to allow extensive AI training on external websites linked on Facebook.” Meta then indefinitely paused that move.

Last month, Etsy also told sellers that it would “set clearer restrictions on AI use,” despite the fact that AI-generated items remain for sale all over the site.

“Today, many active buyers say they can’t tell which items involve AI-generated content,” James Ossman, the company’s vice president of customer operations, wrote on October 22. “It’s become a top-three barrier to shopping more often on Etsy.”

For years, Etsy has been notoriously poor at enforcing its own rules, not only regarding AI but also the official prohibitions on selling sex toys , pornography, and even purported witchcraft spells .

items.title: How data centers are driving a US natural-gas boom
items.summary: In May 2025, my colleague David Rotman wrote a feature story describing how AI could keep us dependent on natural gas. Just 18 months later, I’ve lost count of how many times he’s already been proved right. Sure, it’s technically possible to meet the world’s rising electricity de
items.content:
In May 2025, my colleague David Rotman wrote a feature story describing how AI could keep us dependent on natural gas. Just 18 months later, I’ve lost count of how many times he’s already been proved right.

Sure, it’s technically possible to meet the world’s rising electricity demand with other power sources, including renewables like wind and solar supported by batteries. But the reality in the US so far is that the data center boom is helping to fuel a massive natural-gas resurgence.

Just one example: Plans for the Meta data center in Louisiana that David focused on in his story have expanded, and its power needs have too. The local utility went from three planned natural-gas plants to 10 . And as I wrote in a new story this week, data center developers are now looking beyond the grid and planning to build their own off-grid gas power plants . How did we get here?

If you want to understand the future of the grid, one way to do it is by looking at interconnection queues—lists of power plants that have requested a connection to the system. In recent years these queues have been dominated by renewables like wind and solar power, which are generally the cheapest way to build new energy capacity today.

But there’s been a shift in some places, particularly for PJM, the country’s largest power grid operator, which covers parts of 13 states in an area stretching from Illinois to Washington, DC. PJM has seen a major uptick in natural-gas proposals. In August, the operator announced that it had accepted proposals for 715 total projects with a capacity of over 200 gigawatts to join its queue. Nearly half that total capacity represented natural-gas plants.

If all the projects in the queue were built, it would increase the fossil-fuel share on PJM’s grid from 61% to 67%, according to an analysis by Kevin Kircher , an energy modeler and assistant professor of mechanical engineering at Purdue.

PJM’s queue is reflective of a bigger trend across the US. Natural gas is already the single biggest source of electricity in the country, and it has basically become the default to meet exploding power demand.

This AI-driven rush is already affecting greenhouse-gas emissions for tech companies. Meta’s emissions are up 45% over last year’s, according to the company’s recently released 2026 Sustainability Report . That’s even higher than the jumps from fellow hyperscalers Google ( 18% ), Amazon ( 16% ), and Microsoft ( 25% ). The company is also “reevaluating” its 2030 goal to reach net-zero emissions, according to the report, though there aren’t details about how or when it might reach a decision there.

And there’s another tidbit in that Meta report worth noting: The company said that when the grid can’t deliver power “on the necessary timeline,” it will look to other methods, including building its own on-site power generation.

This fits into a related and growing trend that I’ve been tracking recently: Data center developers are looking to bypass long wait times to hook up to the grid by building their own power plants instead.

It’s not new for large industrial facilities to supply their own power. Chemical plants often have natural-gas infrastructure on-site to generate electricity and heat, for example (though they’re generally connected to the grid as well). Mining operations are often remote, requiring an off-grid power source.

But the desire to come online quickly means there could be a massive boom in off-grid power plants for data centers. Over 100 such facilities have been proposed in the US, with a total capacity of 115 gigawatts (that’s more than double the entire peak power demand of California). The vast majority of these sites have been proposed since the beginning of 2025.

There are alternative ways to help meet growing electricity demand: Wind and solar are inexpensive options, and pairing them with batteries could improve their reliability, for example. I’ve also written before about demand flexibility —efforts to limit power drawn from the grid when demand is high.

Right now, though, the evidence continues to stack up that the AI boom in the US is basically synonymous with a natural-gas boom.

New technology could help cut power losses and reinvent a staple of the grid.

Batteries that swap liquid electrolytes for solid materials promise to charge faster, last longer, and (crucially) run cooler.

As kids, we spent hours tinkering and building and just messing with things. As an adult, I could watch my own young kiddos figure out how certain shapes and movement work all day. Through that play, we improved our problem-solving and language skills, and it’s probably not a stretch to say it was good for our early engineering skills.

In this era of development now, we’re starting to get a taste of that again. We’re experimenting more, and taking in more changes, because it’s all new!

For the last four years at GitHub Universe, we’ve had hackable conference badges. What started as a simple e-ink display for your name and job title morphed into a labor of love for Martin Woodward , VP of Developer Relations. This year, the badge evolved into a device with a color screen, rechargeable battery, accelerometer sensors, and touch-sensitive gaming controls.

The tinkering we’ve seen with the badges has been amazing.
